Since the 2024 presidential election, the S&P 500’s total return climbed more than 25% as of April 20, 2026, despite meaningful volatility along the way.[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_7669) “Investors have overcome concerns about geopolitical conflict and trade announcements and focused on fundamental strength, namely corporate earnings growth,” says Bill Merz, head of capital markets research for U.S. Bank Asset Management Group. S&P 500 companies increased fourth-quarter 2025 revenue by 9.2% and earnings by 13.4%, while first-quarter results are exceeding analyst expectations of 9.6% revenue growth and 13.0% earnings growth.[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_286b) Those fundamentals help explain why investors have continued to buy stocks despite higher oil prices, tariff uncertainty and persistent geopolitical risk. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act ([OBBBA](https://www.usbank.com/wealth-management/financial-perspectives/financial-planning/the-real-impact-of-the-tax-cuts-and-jobs-act.html)) lowered corporate and individual taxes, and federal tax refunds were running approximately $47 billion higher than in 2025 through April 24.[4](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_88e) Earlier Federal Reserve rate cuts also helped support borrowing and spending, giving investors another reason to maintain a constructive market view.
There have been periods like this before under President Trump. · SLB and Halliburton lead the gains, up over 20 percent and 15 percent.
